Messages.Author: jnew...@difsol.com
Messages.Body:
Can Mata Hari play Hand Intervention (plays it as a sabbat vampire, has
a title), or is "titled Sabbat Vampire" meant to be shorthand for
"bishop, archbishop, priscus, or cardinal"?

I assume the former (that the card means literally what it says), but
in light of the Keminitri/Justicar-implies-camarilla ruling, I figured
I'd make sure.

Thanks,
John

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
jnew...@difsol.com wrote:

> Can Mata Hari play Hand Intervention (plays it as a sabbat vampire, has
> a title), or is "titled Sabbat Vampire" meant to be shorthand for
> "bishop, archbishop, priscus, or cardinal"?

The former. Titled and Sabbat = titled Sabbat.
The Baron with Into the Fire would be titled and Sabbat, and would
meet the requirement, for instance.

> I assume the former (that the card means literally what it says), but
> in light of the Keminitri/Justicar-implies-camarilla ruling, I figured
> I'd make sure.

One cannot meet a Justicar requirement without meeting a Camarilla
requirement [10.1] It, too, means literally what it says.

Yes. [10.2]

> What then happens if Lambach has a writ of acceptance and then you play
> into the fire on him?

His underlying "permanent" sect is Sabbat, but he still carries a Writ,
so he's still Camarilla.
